title: Subgraphs & Composition
objective: After this lesson you will be able to extract reusable flows into tested subgraphs, choose supervisor vs sequential multi-agent topologies, and manage cross-graph state contracts without leakage.
why: Single graphs grow into mega-graphs: thirty nodes, inscrutable routing, untestable wholes. Composition (subgraphs as functions, supervisors for dynamic teams, sequential pipelines for fixed flows) restores modularity — and draws the exact boundary the CrewAI multi-agent course starts from. Mega-graphs are monolith prompts at a larger scale.

blocks.text: A **subgraph** is a complete graph (own nodes, edges, tests) embedded as one node in a parent: inputs mapped in, outputs mapped out, internals hidden. The returns flow (triage→decide→draft) becomes a callable unit reused by chat, email, and phone parents. Rules: versioned independently, tested standalone *and* composed, state contract explicit at the boundary (which parent fields enter, which child fields exit).

blocks.caption: mapIn/mapOut are the API signatures of embedded graphs

blocks.text: Supervisor vs sequential: topology by variability

**Sequential**: fixed pipeline (triage→decide→draft→log) — simple, cheap, debuggable; breaks when steps need skipping. **Supervisor**: a router-agent delegating to specialists per step (fraud check sometimes, VIP handling sometimes, escalation on signals) — flexible, costlier, harder to trace. Choose by control-flow variability: fixed → sequential, dynamic → supervisor. Hybrids (sequential backbone, supervisor for exceptions) are the production norm, not a compromise.

blocks.caption: Supervisor loops need termination proofs: caps + done-flags

blocks.text: Composition leaks without contracts: parent fields drifting into child logic, child internals depending on parent extras. Enforce **narrow interfaces** (mapIn picks exactly the needed fields; mapOut returns exactly the promised ones), **namespace child outputs** (`returns.decision`, not bare `decision`), and test composition (parent + real subgraph, not mocks) for contract drift on every version bump.

blocks.title: Compose the returns unit
blocks.note: Run it: expect namespaced outputs per channel with correct paths, and the namespace check true. Same subgraph, two parents, zero leakage — composition without contracts would smear 'decision' across both.

items: Subgraphs = versioned, twice-tested (standalone + composed) reusable flows with explicit mapIn/mapOut
Sequential for fixed pipelines; supervisor for dynamic delegation (with termination proofs); hybrids in production
Narrow namespaced interfaces prevent cross-graph leakage; test composition on version bumps

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice composition and confirm namespacing. (b) Sketch the fraud-check subgraph (inputs: orderId, amount; outputs: risk {low/high}, reasons) with its own routing test. (c) Decide supervisor vs sequential for: order-status lookup bot vs mixed returns+fraud+VIP desk — with the variability argument and termination proof for any loop.
hints: Namespace proof first: returnsDecision present, bare decision absent — leakage check passes.
Fraud subgraph: mapIn picks orderId+amount; outputs risk+reasons namespaced (fraud.risk); standalone tests: low/high/adversarial.
Lookup bot: sequential (fixed: fetch→format→reply). Mixed desk: supervisor (per-ticket delegation varies) with max-rounds + done-flag termination.
exercise.why: Reuse (subgraph extraction), topology choice (variability analysis), and loop safety (termination proofs) are the three composition judgments — each decided on concrete systems, with contracts preventing the leakage that kills modular designs.
exercise.code: // Composition checklist: mapIn/mapOut narrow + namespaced, tested standalone + composed.

quiz.q: Same returns flow needed in chat, email, phone bots. Approach?
options: Subgraph: versioned, tested standalone + composed, mapped in/out with namespaced outputs
quiz.explain: Subgraphs are reuse without duplication: test once, compose thrice, contracts prevent leakage. Copies diverge; mega-graphs tangle.

quiz.q: Supervisor loop without max-rounds or done-flag. Risk?
options: Unbounded delegation loops hang: termination needs caps + done-flags by construction
quiz.explain: Dynamic delegation can cycle (A→B→A). Termination proofs (caps, flags) are structural requirements, not optimizations.

quiz.q: Child graph reads parent's raw ticket directly instead of mapped inputs. Problem?
options: Contract leakage: undeclared coupling breaks reuse and versioning — narrow mapIn/mapOut interfaces only
quiz.explain: Undeclared reads couple child to parent internals: reuse elsewhere breaks silently. Narrow explicit interfaces keep composition modular.

summary: Subgraphs for reuse (tested twice, versioned, namespaced), supervisor vs sequential by variability (termination proved), contracts against leakage. Composition turns graphs into teams — the CrewAI course continues here.
next: Composed teams need proof: traces, gold conversations, and per-segment diffs. Next: evaluating graphs end to end.
